title: Enhancing Generalization in Large-Scale HCVRP: A Rank-Augmented Neural Solver

problem.claim: HCVRP is an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem.

gap.claim: Neural solvers trained on small-scale instances struggle to generalize to large-scale scenarios.

contributions.claim: RANS increases and approximates the upper bound of the attention matrix rank to generate more distinctive node features.
RANS uses a Dual Cross-Attention Module in the vehicle encoder to capture each vehicle's optimal routes while maintaining balanced vehicle collaboration.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose RANS with two stated innovations: rank augmentation and a Dual Cross-Attention Module.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that RANS performs favorably against the baselines.
On instances with up to 10,000 nodes, the authors report that RANS uses 13.42% of the best baseline neural solver's inference time and reduces min-max travel time by 23.72%.

narrative_sequence.summary: HCVRP is framed as an NP-hard combinatorial optimization problem.
Existing neural solvers have difficulty generalizing from small-scale training to large-scale scenarios.
The abstract attributes performance degradation to low-rank attention matrices, insufficient node-feature distinction, and excessive cross-vehicle feature incorporation.
RANS addresses the stated challenges through rank augmentation and Dual Cross-Attention.
The authors report favorable baseline comparisons and efficiency and travel-time improvements on instances up to 10,000 nodes.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links large-scale generalization degradation to low-rank attention and weak distinction among node features.

interpretation.claim: Representation capacity in attention may be a bottleneck when scaling neural combinatorial optimization models.

application.claim: For similar large-scale routing models, inspect attention-rank behavior and feature distinguishability when diagnosing generalization failures.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the same bottleneck applies across other problem classes, architectures, or training regimes.

unknowns: Training setup, data generation, and dataset composition are not specified.
Baseline identities and evaluation protocols are not specified.
The abstract does not provide statistical variation, ablations, or details supporting the reported improvements.
